newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SABENA HIKES SOME FARES, VIRGIN EXPRESS SAYS NO.
newsitem.headline: SABENA HIKES SOME FARES, VIRGIN EXPRESS SAYS NO.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena said on Wednesday it would hike the full fare for its flights to London and Manchester by 2.5 percent in response to a similar increase by British Airways Plc (BA).
BA is putting up prices of its flights on European routes due to higher fuel costs.
"We'll follow (BA's) decision with immediate effect for London and Manchester, BA's main connections between Brussels and England," Sabena spokesman Erik Sclep said.

Richard Branson's Virgin Express European regional airline by contrast will not raise fares for now, its chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein said. "We don't have any immediate plans to raise fares."

BA earlier said it would increase full published fares on its European routes by 2.5 percent on average from mid-October due to a 30 percent rise in jet fuel cost since mid-July. BA said it was also considering increases on long-haul routes.
Sclep said Sabena, 49.5 percent owned by Swissair , would not yet increase fares for other destinations.
"If there are important changes by important carriers on stretches to Brussels, we'll probably follow," he said.

Brussels-based Virgin Express might reconsider if jet fuel prices would stay high or go even higher. "But I'm not certain that raising fares at this point is what we want to do, especially since we're going into the winter," Ornstein said.
"The higher the fare the lower the traffic and if things slow down you want to put as many people on the plane as you can," he said.

Virgin Express was barely competing with BA. "I don't think we compete with BA anywhere on our system, except perhaps on one trip a day from Brussels to Rome (but) I don't think we're going to raise that fare," he said.
